question_groups.title: EMC assessment and technical documentation (Annex I, Annex II)

questions.label: What kind of equipment is the product under the EMC Directive?
questions.guidance: Apparatus is a finished appliance, or a combination of them, made available on the market as a single functional unit, intended for the end-user and liable to generate electromagnetic disturbance or affected by it. A fixed installation is a particular combination of several types of apparatus and, where applicable, other devices, assembled, installed and intended to be used permanently at a predefined location. Excluded by the directive: equipment whose inherent physical characteristics make it incapable of generating or contributing to emissions that exceed a level allowing radio, telecommunication and other equipment to operate as intended, and which also works without unacceptable degradation in the disturbance normally to be expected in its intended use (both parts must hold); radio equipment used by radio amateurs, unless made available on the market (kits of components for radio amateurs to assemble do not count as made available); and custom-built evaluation kits for professionals, used only at research and development facilities. A component or sub-assembly that its maker only builds into other equipment, with no direct function for an end-user, is not apparatus under the Commission's EMC Guide.

questions.label: How do you show that the apparatus meets the EMC protection requirements?
questions.guidance: Harmonised standards cited in the Official Journal give a presumption of conformity for the phenomena they cover. Where none is applied, or only part of it, your EMC assessment and technical documentation must show how the protection requirements are met.

questions.label: Is the apparatus accompanied by information on the specific precautions to take when it is assembled, installed, maintained or used, and, where compliance is not ensured in residential areas, by a clear indication of that restriction of use?
questions.guidance: The aim is that the apparatus is in conformity with the Annex I(1) protection requirements when put into service. The restriction of use is also shown on the packaging where appropriate, and the information needed to use the apparatus as intended goes in the instructions that accompany it.

questions.label: Are the good engineering practices applied to the fixed installation documented, with the documentation kept at the disposal of the national authorities for as long as the installation is in operation?
questions.guidance: A fixed installation has no CE marking or EU declaration of conformity. It must be installed with good engineering practices, respecting the information on the intended use of its components. The documentation is held by the person or persons responsible, whom the Member States identify under their own rules.

requirements.label: Design and manufacture the equipment, having regard to the state of the art, so that the electromagnetic disturbance it generates does not exceed the level above which radio and telecommunications equipment or other equipment cannot operate as intended

Design and manufacture the equipment so that it has a level of immunity to the electromagnetic disturbance to be expected in its intended use, which allows it to operate without unacceptable degradation of its intended use

Carry out the electromagnetic compatibility assessment of the apparatus on the basis of the relevant phenomena, covering all normal intended operating conditions and every configuration the manufacturer identifies as representative, and establish the technical documentation, including an analysis and assessment of the risks
Draw up the EU declaration of conformity once compliance is demonstrated, keep it up to date, and draw up a single one where several Union acts require it
Affix the CE marking visibly, legibly and indelibly before the apparatus is placed on the market
Keep the technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity for 10 years after the apparatus has been placed on the market
Keep series production in conformity, taking changes in design or characteristics and in harmonised standards or other technical specifications into account

Mark a type, batch or serial number or other element allowing identification, or, where the size or nature of the apparatus does not allow it, give that information on the packaging or in a document accompanying the apparatus

Indicate your name, registered trade name or registered trade mark and a single postal address at which you can be contacted, on the apparatus or, where that is not possible, on its packaging or in a document accompanying it

Supply the instructions and the information on the use of the apparatus required by Art. 18, in a language easily understood by consumers and other end-users as determined by the Member State, clear, understandable and intelligible
Immediately take the corrective measures needed to bring non-conforming apparatus into conformity, or withdraw or recall it, and inform the competent national authorities where it presents a risk
Give the competent authority, on reasoned request, the information and documentation needed to demonstrate conformity, and cooperate on eliminating risks

Under the mandate: keep the EU declaration of conformity and technical documentation at the disposal of the market surveillance authorities for 10 years after the apparatus has been placed on the market, provide information and documentation on reasoned request, and cooperate with the authorities
Place only compliant apparatus on the market

Before placing apparatus on the market, ensure that the manufacturer has carried out the conformity assessment procedure, drawn up the technical documentation, affixed the CE marking, supplied the required documents and complied with Art. 7(5) and (6); do not place non-conforming apparatus on the market and inform the manufacturer and the authorities of any risk
Indicate your name, registered trade name or registered trade mark and postal address on the apparatus or, where that is not possible, on its packaging or in a document accompanying it
Ensure the apparatus is accompanied by the instructions and the Art. 18 information in a language easily understood by consumers and other end-users as determined by the Member State
Ensure that storage and transport conditions do not jeopardise compliance with the essential requirements
Immediately take the corrective measures needed to bring non-conforming apparatus into conformity, or withdraw or recall it, and inform the competent national authorities where it presents a risk

For 10 years after the apparatus has been placed on the market, keep a copy of the EU declaration of conformity at the disposal of the market surveillance authorities and ensure the technical documentation can be made available to them on request
Give the competent authority, on reasoned request, the information and documentation needed to demonstrate conformity, and cooperate on eliminating risks
Act with due care in relation to the requirements of the directive

Before making apparatus available, verify the CE marking, the required documents, the instructions and Art. 18 information in a language understood in the Member State of supply, and that the manufacturer and importer have complied with Art. 7(5) and (6) and Art. 9(3)
Ensure that storage and transport conditions do not jeopardise compliance with the essential requirements
Make sure the corrective measures needed for non-conforming apparatus are taken, and inform the competent national authorities where it presents a risk
Give the competent authority, on reasoned request, the information and documentation needed to demonstrate conformity, and cooperate on eliminating risks

On request, identify to the market surveillance authorities the economic operators who supplied you and those you supplied, for 10 years after you were supplied and for 10 years after you supplied the apparatus
Install the fixed installation applying good engineering practices and respecting the information on the intended use of its components, with a view to meeting the Annex I(1) requirements

Document the good engineering practices applied and hold the documentation, as the person responsible, at the disposal of the national authorities for inspection for as long as the fixed installation is in operation

finding_rules.message: Radio equipment: electromagnetic compatibility is assessed under RED Art. 3(1)(b), not the EMC Directive. Use the RED package.

Radio hardware present but disabled (physically, or until a manufacturer update): the product is under the EMC Directive, not RED, while the radio stays disabled. Enabling it makes the product radio equipment and requires re-assessment under RED.

Radio equipment used exclusively for defence or public or State security is outside RED, so its EMC falls back to the EMC Directive. A Member State may set EU product rules aside for its essential security interests (Art. 346 TFEU): check the national rules and the procurement terms.

Excluded from the EMC Directive by Art. 2(2), or by the Commission EMC Guide's reading of the definition of apparatus (components). Keep the reasoning on record, for example why the equipment can neither cause nor suffer disturbance, because the authorities can ask for it.

Fixed installation: no CE marking or EU declaration of conformity. Apparatus that is also made available on the market must meet the directive on its own. Apparatus made only for this installation need not, but its documentation must identify the installation and the precautions for incorporating it.
Document the good engineering practices applied to the fixed installation, and hold the documentation at the disposal of the national authorities for as long as the installation is in operation.
No presumption of conformity for the phenomena not covered by harmonised standards: the EMC assessment and technical documentation must show how the protection requirements are met for them.
Complete the technical documentation, including the EMC assessment, before placing the apparatus on the market.
Arrange to keep the technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity for 10 years after the apparatus has been placed on the market.
Draw up the EU declaration of conformity before placing the apparatus on the market.
Affix the CE marking before placing the apparatus on the market.

Mark a type, batch or serial number and the manufacturer's name and postal address on the units. Where the size or nature of the apparatus does not allow it, give the information on the packaging or in a document accompanying the apparatus.

Supply the Art. 18 information with the apparatus: the specific precautions for assembly, installation, maintenance and use, and a clear indication of any restriction of use in residential areas, also on the packaging where appropriate.
Check the CE marking, the documents and instructions and the identification of the manufacturer and importer before supplying the apparatus.
Placing the apparatus under your own name or modifying it makes you the manufacturer: the manufacturer's obligations apply to you.
Open-source steward is not a role under the EMC Directive. Answer as manufacturer, importer, distributor or authorised representative for this product.
All units were placed on the market before 20 April 2016: they may still be made available if they conform to the previous directive, 2004/108/EC.
